cold: Day thirty. Midnight. Every zombie in the county came for the fireworks.
You're in a balloon that has never flown. And the rope is still tied.
d01: Day one. Starfall Park, the biggest theme park on Silver Lake.
You're seventeen, and your summer job is Rascal the Raccoon. Giant head, fur suit, ninety degrees.
At noon, the Thunderbolt roller coaster comes back with one rider who isn't screaming anymore. He bites the man next to him.
Ten minutes later, the whole park is running. You can't run in raccoon feet.
They catch up. And then they walk right past you.
d02: Day two. You wake up in the costume room. Something is eating your sandwich.
A real raccoon. She looks at you, then at your costume, and decides you're her mom. You call her Bandit.
Outside, the gates are chained. The only bridge to town is jammed with cars, and worse.
Starfall Park is an island now. And you're on it.
d03: Day three. You figure out why they walked past you.
Rule number one. They hunt by smell. And Rascal smells like thirty summers of popcorn and sweat.
Inside the costume, you're invisible. You walk through a crowd of a thousand of them, all the way to the hot dog stand.
Nobody even looks at you. Best disguise in the world.
d04: Day four. Rule number two, by accident.
Bandit jumps on the control panel, and the carousel starts playing music.
Every head in the park turns. And they come. Hundreds of them stumble onto the spinning platform.
Rule two. They follow music. And now three hundred of them are riding the carousel. Round and round.
d05: Day five. Rule number three. They can't climb. Not ladders, not fences, not even the kiddie slide.
So you go up. Above the park, there's a whole other world. Catwalks, coaster tracks, and the Sky Ride.
Little buckets on a cable, from one end of the park to the other.
Your own private highway in the sky.
d06: Day six. The ride operators' radios still work. You try every channel.
On channel nine, somebody answers. This is Gus.
He's seventy-four. He built the Thunderbolt in nineteen seventy-nine, and he flew the park's sky balloon for thirty years.
He lives in the old lighthouse across the lake. Wave, he says. You wave. A tiny light blinks back.
d07: Day seven. One week alive. That deserves a party.
Cotton candy as big as your head. Ice cream for breakfast. Every ride, no line.
You ride the Thunderbolt eleven times in a row.
Bandit eats three funnel cakes and falls asleep in a spinning teacup. Best party ever. Guest list: one raccoon.
d08: Day eight. The ring toss at the arcade.
All summer, you tried to win the giant rainbow unicorn for your little sister, Lily. You promised her.
Today, nobody can stop you from practicing. Two hundred rings later, it's yours.
It's taller than you. Now you just have to get it home.
d09: Day nine. Gus has bad news.
The park's computer is still running the summer schedule. On day thirty, at midnight, it fires the biggest fireworks show in the state. By itself.
Every zombie for fifty miles will hear it. They'll come across the bridge. All of them.
Then I'll leave before that, you say. Kid, says Gus, there's only one way off that island now. Up.
d10: Day ten. The Sky Balloon. A giant striped balloon on a rope, folded in a shed for ten years.
Mice ate the ropes. The burner is rusty. The fabric has thirty-seven holes.
And it has never once flown without a rope tying it to the ground.
Twenty days. You'd better learn fast.
d11: Day eleven. Lesson one. Gus says a balloon is just a big bag of hot air, and a little bit of courage.
You build a tiny one, out of a trash bag and a birthday candle.
It rises. It floats over the park. And it lands on a zombie's head.
Lesson one, it works. Lesson two, you can't steer.
d12: Day twelve. Thirty-seven holes need patches, and the only fabric in the park is costumes.
The dragon. The cow. The dancing hot dog. You cut them all up.
You sew all night. Bandit steals the thread.
By morning, the balloon looks like a zoo exploded on it. Thirteen holes fixed.
d13: Day thirteen. You catch Rascal on a fence, and it rips. A hole, right in your side.
For the first time, they smell you.
You run into the mirror maze. A hundred of you. A hundred of them.
You make it out the back door, and sew Rascal shut with balloon fabric. Now you're a raccoon with a rainbow patch.
d14: Day fourteen. Halfway. You have a routine.
Sky Ride to the balloon shed at sunrise. Sewing until noon. Burner practice in the afternoon.
At eight, Gus on the radio, and a flashlight blinking across the lake.
You sleep in the tower of the fairy tale castle, with a raccoon on your feet. Patches, twenty-five out of thirty-seven.
d15: Day fifteen. The burner needs propane, and the tanks are empty.
But behind the food court, there are forty full tanks for the grills. On Main Street. Where four hundred of them live.
Costume on. You roll the tanks one by one, slowly, right through the crowd.
One tank clanks. Every head turns. You freeze. Rascal waves. They turn back.
d16: Day sixteen. Forty tanks, and they're heavy. The balloon shed is on the other side of the lagoon.
But the log flume still runs.
You load every tank into a log, and send them down the big drop, one after another.
Splash, splash, splash. Forty tanks in the lagoon, right next to the shed. Zero lost.
d17: Day seventeen. You climb to the top of the Big Wheel, the highest point in the park.
From up here, you see everything. The jammed bridge. The town, full of them. And the lake. Four miles of water.
On the far shore, the lighthouse. Gus flashes his light three times.
That's how far you have to fly.
d18: Day eighteen. The basket needs new ropes. Strong ones.
The strongest rope in the park is the steel cable of the Zip Line, over the lagoon.
You ride it one last time. Faster than you've ever gone, screaming the whole way.
Then you cut it down. Eight hundred feet of cable, and a very good day.
d19: Day nineteen. The first inflation test, at night, in the Kiddie Land field.
Fan on. Burner on. And slowly, the balloon stands up. Huge, glowing, covered in dragon wings and cow spots.
It's beautiful. It's also the brightest, loudest thing for miles.
They come. You pull the vent, and the balloon falls flat, right on top of thirty of them.
d20: Day twenty. The balloon needs a safe place, with walls. The castle courtyard.
But it's half a mile away, and it weighs as much as a car.
Rule two. You switch on the parade music, and every zombie on Main Street follows the floats.
You load the balloon onto the last float, and ride it all the way to the castle, waving like a mascot.
d21: You find her at the top of the Thunderbolt's lift hill. Two hundred feet up, crying.
You climb the maintenance ladder. They can't follow. At the top, you find out why she's there.
Three baby raccoons. Bandit is a mom. You carry the whole family down, inside Rascal's head.
d22: Day twenty-two. Gus does the math. The balloon can lift you, the burner, four tanks, and not much else.
You, a raccoon, three babies, a giant unicorn, and a forty-pound costume.
You look at the unicorn. You look at Bandit. You look at Rascal, for a long time.
d23: Day twenty-three. A storm comes off the lake.
Lightning hits the drop tower, and half the park goes dark.
In the control room, the fireworks computer switches to battery. The countdown doesn't even blink.
Seven days. Twelve hours. Six minutes.
d24: Day twenty-four. The storm tore the balloon off its cart, and dropped it in the castle moat.
Three hundred pounds of wet fabric. It will never dry in time.
Unless you hang it on the Swing Ride, and turn it on full speed.
The biggest clothes dryer in the world. Dry by lunch.
d25: Day twenty-five. The plan, with Gus.
At midnight on day thirty, the fireworks start, and every zombie in the park will look up.
That night, the wind blows west. Straight across the lake, to the lighthouse. Four miles. Thirty minutes in the air.
And if the wind changes, you ask. Then you swim, kid.
d26: Day twenty-six. The castle has one gate, and when the fireworks start, ten thousand of them will be in the park.
Rule two, one more time. You wire every speaker on the far side of the park to start at midnight. The carousel, the bumper cars, the parade.
The loudest party on the island. And you won't be there.
d27: Day twenty-seven. You make your choice.
Bandit and her babies are coming. Lily's unicorn is coming. You promised.
You hang the costume on the carousel, and say thank you. For thirty days, it kept you invisible. On day thirty, you're on your own.
d28: Day twenty-eight. At midnight, the fireworks computer fires one test rocket. Bang.
Far across the bridge, the town hears it.
By morning, the bridge is moving. Thousands of them, two days early.
d29: You turn on the Big Wheel lights one last time, and ride it to the top, with Bandit and the babies.
Below you, the park is full of them. Ten thousand faces in the dark.
Across the lake, Gus blinks his light. Get some sleep, kid. You don't.
d30: Day thirty. Midnight. The sky explodes.
Ten thousand heads look up. Then the carousel music starts at the far end of the park, and they turn.
You run for the courtyard. No costume. For the first time in thirty days, they smell you.
Full flame. The balloon pulls up, and stops. The rope. The knot is stuck.
Bandit chews through it in two seconds. She's been practicing for a month.
epi: The balloon lands in the lake, ten feet from the lighthouse. Gus is waiting with a blanket.
A week later, Lily gets a unicorn taller than she is. And a raccoon family in the backyard.
